clues: This city sits by a deep bay on the north coast of a big island in a warm sea. Ships reach its safe port through a slim gap in the coast.
Steady trade winds and warm sea flows keep the heat mild here. Great storms hit the island at times, but they strike the south coast most, not this north shore.
Its fine harbour won this city the capital job in 1552. It took the role from Santiago, which had held it before.
Old cars from the 1950s still cruise the Malecón, the long sea wall road. With no fresh parts for years, clever hands keep them running with bits from home.
Cuba's government sits in this city, and its ministries work here too. More than 100 foreign offices are based in its streets too.
